key_insight: This paper presents a brain-inspired generative model that can imagine future possibilities and plan toward goals using neural sampling from cognitive maps. The key advance is that complex planning and problem-solving emerge from simple local learning rules rather than heavy global optimization.
problem_solved: The paper addresses how AI systems can perform goal-directed imagination and planning in a way that is both flexible and biologically plausible. It targets the challenge of building models that combine compositional reasoning, uncertainty, and efficient learning with local synaptic plasticity.
method: Uses cognitive maps to represent structured knowledge about states, goals, and relationships.
Employs stochastic neural sampling to generate candidate future trajectories and possible solutions.
Encodes information compositionally so new plans can be built from reusable components.
Relies only on local synaptic plasticity, avoiding the need for complex global training signals.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a pathway to more efficient, interpretable, and flexible planning systems inspired by the brain. It may be especially relevant for robotics, decision-making, and agents that need to reason under uncertainty with limited training supervision.
visual_elements: A flow diagram showing cognitive map -> neural sampling -> imagined trajectories -> goal-directed plan
A side-by-side comparison of local synaptic plasticity versus global optimization-based learning
An illustration of compositional code blocks assembling different plans from shared components
A trajectory map with multiple stochastic paths converging on a target goal
paper_title: Neural sampling from cognitive maps enables goal-directed imagination and planning
paper_authors: Hui Lin, Yukun Yang, Rong Zhao, Giovanni Pezzulo, Wolfgang Maass
